o.text: Borrowed from Russian шкаф (škaf), from a Germanic language.
Borrowed from Russian лими́т (limít), itself from French limite.
Internationalism; from Russian жанр (žanr), ultimately from French genre.
Borrowed from Turkish döner, from Turkish döner kebap, from dönmek + kebap. Cognate with Azerbaijani dönmək (“to (re)turn”).

Analyzable as zol + -aq.
Compare Turkmen zolak, Crimean Tatar yolaq/colaq (Northern Dialect), Kumyk ёлакъ (yolaq, “stain”), Kazakh жолақ (jolaq).
